What should I do if there is an accident at home or school?

Very important question! If an accident happens, stay calm and do not panic. First, call an adult immediately: a parent, teacher or any trusted grown-up nearby. Do not try to treat a serious injury yourself. If someone is bleeding a little, a clean cloth can be pressed gently on the cut while you wait for help. Do not move a person who has fallen badly, because moving them wrongly can cause more harm. Keep other children away from danger, like broken glass or fire. Remember: shout for help, stay calm, and let adults handle it. You could save a life!

What are the important emergency phone numbers I should know?

Well done for asking! Every child should know these numbers. The national emergency number in Nigeria is 112; it is free to call from any network, even without airtime, and connects you to the police, fire service and ambulance. You should also memorise the phone number of your parent or guardian, so you can reach them if you are lost or in trouble. Some states have their own emergency lines too, like 767 in Lagos. Only call these numbers for real emergencies; calling to play is wrong and can block help from reaching someone in danger. Write 112 in your exercise book today!

What should I do if I get lost in a market or a strange place?

Good question, this can happen to anyone! If you get lost, first stop walking and stay calm; do not wander further, because moving around makes it harder for your family to find you. Look around for a safe helper: a police officer, a security guard, a market leader, or a mother with children. Tell them your name, your parents' names and their phone number if you know it. This is why memorising a parent's phone number is so important. Never follow a stranger who promises to take you home, and never enter a stranger's car. Stay where people can see you. Stay safe!

How can I stay safe on the road?

Very wise question! Road safety saves lives every day. Always look left, look right, and look left again before crossing the road, and cross only when it is clear. Use the zebra crossing or pedestrian bridge where there is one. Never play, run or push your friends on or near the road. Walk on the side of the road facing oncoming vehicles, so you can see cars coming. Obey traffic lights and the traffic warden. Do not chase a ball onto the road; let an adult help you get it. In a vehicle, sit properly and do not put your head or hands outside the window. Be road-wise!

What should I do if there is a fire?

Very important question! If you see a fire, shout 'Fire! Fire!' to alert everyone, and leave the building quickly through the nearest safe exit. Do not stop to pick your bag or toys; your life is worth more than any property. Do not hide under beds or inside cupboards. If the room is smoky, bend low or crawl, because cleaner air stays near the floor. If your clothes catch fire, remember: stop, drop and roll on the ground to put it out. Once outside, stay out, and let adults call the fire service on 112. Never play with matches, lighters, candles or petrol. Fire is not a toy!

Who can I ask for help when I feel unsafe?

This is a very important question, and I am glad you asked! Every child has the right to protection, and you should never suffer in silence. If you feel unsafe or someone is hurting you or touching you wrongly, tell a trusted adult immediately: your parents, your class teacher, the headteacher, a school counsellor, or a religious leader you trust. If the first person does not listen, tell another one; keep telling until someone helps you. You can also call 112 in an emergency. You are never at fault for reporting, and telling is not being a bad child; it is being brave and wise. You deserve to be safe!

How can I avoid danger from strangers?

Very wise question! Most people are good, but we must still be careful with strangers. Never collect sweets, biscuits, money or gifts from someone you do not know. Never follow a stranger anywhere, even if they say your mummy sent them; families should agree on a secret word for real emergencies. Never enter a stranger's car or house. Do not tell strangers your home address or when your parents are away. Walk to and from school with friends or trusted adults, and use busy roads, not lonely paths. If a stranger grabs you, shout loudly and run to where people are. Always tell your parents about any stranger who approaches you!

Why should I not play with electricity?

Excellent safety question! Electricity is very useful, but it can injure or even kill when handled carelessly. Never push your fingers, pencils, spoons or wires into electric sockets. Do not touch switches, sockets or electrical appliances with wet hands, because water carries electric current easily. Do not fly kites near electric wires, and never touch a fallen electric cable on the road; report it to an adult at once. If an appliance sparks or smells like it is burning, move away and tell an adult immediately. Let only adults and electricians handle electrical repairs. Respect electricity and it will serve you safely!
